questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: A 35-year-old man came with complaints of dark-colored stools to the OPD. After undergoing endoscopy, the patient was diagnosed with an upper GI bleed. Which of the following structures is used as a demarcation point to differentiate it from a lower GI bleed?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Ligament of Treitz

The ligament of Treitz is used as the demarcation point to differentiate between upper gastrointestinal bleeding and lower gastrointestinal bleeding. It is a part of the duodenojejunal junction.

Upper GI bleeding refers to bleeding proximal to the ligament of Treitz, and lower GI bleeding refers to bleeding distal to the ligament of Treitz.
questions.learning: Ligament of Treitz — The ligament of Treitz is used as the demarcation point to differentiate between upper gastrointestinal bleeding and lower gastrointestinal bleeding.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: A 34-year-old woman who works as a housemaid presents with knee pain and swelling, a condition commonly linked to repetitive kneeling and prolonged pressure. In housemaid’s knee, which specific area of the knee is typically affected?
questions.explanation: The condition known as "Housemaid's knee" refers to prepatellar bursitis. This clinical entity is an inflammation of the prepatellar bursa, which is located superficially between the skin and the patella. It is caused by repetitive friction or direct pressure from frequent kneeling, which is common in occupations such as house cleaning. This leads to localized swelling and tenderness directly over the kneecap. Suprapatellar bursa (Option A) is an extension of the knee joint cavity above the patella and is usually affected by joint effusions. Infrapatellar bursa (Option C) is located below the patella and is associated with "Clergyman’s knee," often seen in individuals who kneel more upright. The Pes Anserine bursa (Option D) is located on the medial side of the proximal tibia and is usually associated with runners or those with osteoarthritis. Therefore, label B identifies the specific area damaged in this patient
questions.learning: The condition known as "Housemaid's knee" refers to prepatellar bursitis. This clinical entity is an inflammation of the prepatellar bursa, which is located superficially between the skin and the patella.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Dr. Sarah made a presentation on Infectious diseases. She spoke about the prevention and treatment of Zika virus. Which of the following is true with respect to the prevention and treatment of Zika virus?
options: Sexual abstinence, using condoms, and delaying pregnancy helps control the disease
Purified, inactivated FDA-approved vaccine is found to be helpful in prevention
Immunoglobulin and plasmapheresis are used in the treatment of Zika
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Sexual abstinence, using condoms, and delaying pregnancy helps control the disease

Sexual abstinence, using condoms, and delaying pregnancy help control Zika virus infections.

Zika virus can be transmitted by the bite of infected Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. Zika virus belongs to the Flaviviridae family. It is an arbovirus that is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, primarily Aedes aegypti. The reservoir of infection is unknown and has not yet been reported in India. Zika virus can also be transmitted via sexual contact, blood transfusion, and also from mother to fetus during pregnancy.

Infection with Zika virus is usually asymptomatic. The symptoms are usually mild and include fever, skin rashes, conjunctivitis, and muscle and joint pain. These symptoms usually resolve in 2-7 days. Complications include Guillain-Barré syndrome, neuropathy, and myelitis, and are particularly seen in adults and older children.

Zika virus infection during pregnancy is associated with complications such as fetal loss, preterm birth, and stillbirth. The transmission of the infection to the baby can lead to congenital Zika syndrome which is characterized by microcephaly. Other malformations include limb contractures, high muscle tone, eye abnormalities, and hearing loss. Congenital malformations can follow both symptomatic and asymptomatic infections.

RT-PCR is the standard test for the diagnosis of Zika virus infection. In India, NCDC Delhi and the National Institute of Virology Pune, are the only institutes that can provide the diagnosis in an acute febrile stage.

There is no treatment available for Zika virus infection(options C & D). Plenty of rest and fluids along with antipyretics and/or analgesics are indicated for symptom relief. Medical attention should be sought if symptoms worsen. There is no vaccine available for the prevention of Zika virus infection(option B). The key measure for prevention is protection against mosquito bites. WHO also recommends contraceptive counselling for sexually active men and women, especially in regions with active Zika virus transmission.

The image below depicts the transplacental transmission of Zika virus infection.
questions.learning: Sexual abstinence, using condoms, and delaying pregnancy helps control the disease Sexual abstinence, using condoms, and delaying pregnancy help control Zika virus infections.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: The manoeuvre marked with an asterisk shown in the following image is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Pringle

The image shows compression/clamping of the hepatoduodenal ligament at the porta hepatis, which is the Pringle manoeuvre.

The Pringle manoeuvre temporarily occludes the portal triad:

• Proper hepatic artery
• Portal vein
• Common bile duct

It is used during liver surgery or severe hepatic trauma to reduce hepatic inflow and control bleeding.

Why not the other options?

• A. Mattox: Left-sided abdominal visceral rotation to expose the retroperitoneum and major vessels.
• B. Kocher: Mobilization of the duodenum and pancreatic head by incising the lateral peritoneal attachment.
• C. Shoe-shine: Technique used during liver resection to mobilize/dissect liver tissue.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: A patient presents with weight gain, thinning of hair, and dry skin. The clinical features are suggestive of Hashimoto's thyroiditis. Which of the following antibodies is most commonly associated with this condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Anti-thyroid peroxidase antibody

Hashimoto’s thyroiditis is the most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient areas. An elevated TSH and the presence of thyroid peroxidase antibodies usually confirm the diagnosis.

It is an autoimmune disease (associated with HLA DR-3 and HLA-B8) that results in the destruction of the thyroid gland and gradual and progressive thyroid failure. The most commonly associated antibody is anti-thyroid peroxidase antibody (Anti-TPO), which targets the enzyme thyroid peroxidase, essential for thyroid hormone synthesis.

Clinical features of Hashimoto's thyroiditis are as follows:

* More common in women (10 to 20 times)

* Diffusely enlarged, painless, lobulated gland

* Patients usually present with hypothyroidism (due to alteration in thyroid function by infiltration of lymphocytes and resultant fibrosis)

* Hashitoxicosis: initial transient phase of thyrotoxicosis

Laboratory investigations show,

* Elevated TSH

* Low T3 and T4

* Presence of thyroid autoantibodies-

* Anti-thyroid peroxidase (Anti-TPO)

* Antithyroglobulin (Anti-Tg)

* Thyrotropin Receptor Antibody (Anti-TSH-R)

* Anti sodium/iodide symporter (Anti-NIS)

The management of Hashimoto's thyroiditis is as follows:

* Thyroid hormone replacement therapy

The algorithm used for Thyroid hormone replacement therapy in Hashimoto's thyroiditis is as shown below,

Surgery may be required if there is a suspicion of malignancy or goiters causing compressive symptoms.

Note: All the other options (Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI), TSH receptor antibodies (TSHR-Ab), Long-acting thyroid stimulator) are antibodies that are primarily associated with Graves’ disease, leading to hyperthyroidism

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Hospital management wants to estimate the average time a doctor spends with each patient to decide whether staffing levels need adjustment. Which management technique would be most suitable for assessing this?
questions.explanation: Work sampling is a statistical management technique used to analyze the time spent by workers on various categories of tasks. It involves making a large number of instantaneous observations at random intervals to determine what proportion of a worker's time is dedicated to specific activities, such as patient interaction. This is the most appropriate method for determining average interaction duration because it provides objective data without the continuous presence of an observer. Option A refers to theoretical simulations. Option B is a broad administrative process rather than a measurement tool. Option C involves hiring, training, and policy development rather than time-task analysis. Work sampling allows hospital management to identify workflow bottlenecks and justify staffing adjustments to enhance the quality of care. By quantifying non-repetitive work, it helps in optimizing the ratio of clinicians to patients, ensuring that the health system functions efficiently and meets patient needs

questions.subject: Ophthalmology
questions.text: The SAFE strategy given by WHO forms the mainstay of the management of trachoma. What does the S in this acronym represent?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Surgery

The S in the acronym stands for surgery.

Trachoma is treated according to the WHO classification using the SAFEstrategy (Surgery, Antibiotics, Facial hygiene, and Environmental improvement). Azithromycin is the antibiotic of choice, and surgery involves the correction of trichiasis and entropion. In case of significant corneal scarring, penetrating keratoplasty is done.

Trachoma is a form of chronic infective conjunctivitis and is one of the leading causes of blindness. It is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis, more specifically the TRIC (trachoma inclusion conjunctivitis) serovars A, B, Ba, C. It has an ‘active’ inflammatory stage and a ‘cicatricial’ chronic stage. The active inflammatory stage is more prevalent in children and presents with nonspecific symptoms of ocular irritation, foreign body sensation, and discharge (often mild symptoms). Examination findings at this stage show:

* Conjunctival follicles contain Leber cells (multinucleated lymphocytes)

* Corneal Herbert's follicles (similar to conjunctival follicles)

The cicatricial chronic stage is seen in middle age. The patient complains of pain, lacrimation, photophobia and later blurring, and finally loss of vision. Conjunctiva shows concretions (whitish deposits of inspissated mucus in depressions called glands of Henle). Corneal signs include:

* Herbert pits (pitted scars in the limbal which are remnants of healed Herbert follicles)

* Corneal opacity is seen in later stages.

The below image shows Herbert's pits.

There can be associated trichiasis ( when at least one eyelash rubs the eyeball) and entropion.

At present WHO grading with `FISTO’ is in use.

Pearl PF1843: WHO Programme to Control Trachoma: SAFE Strategy

* S—Surgery: Trichiasis and entropion correction surgery → 3° prevention.

* A—Antibiotics: Oral azithromycin, topical 1% tetracycline, topical 1% azithromycin → 2° prevention

* F—Facial hygiene → 1° prevention.

* E—Environmental cleanliness → primordial prevention

The strategy depends on the prevalence of trachoma follicle in children (aged 1–9 yrs)

* >10% → Mass antibiotic treatment at the community level and FE measures

* 5 to 10% → Targeted antibiotic treatment (affected families) and FE measures

* < 5% → FE measures
questions.learning: Surgery — The S in the acronym stands for surgery. Trachoma is treated according to the WHO classification using the SAFEstrategy (Surgery, Antibiotics, Facial hygiene, and Environmental improvement).

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.text: A 49-year-old male presents with recurrent episodes of watery diarrhea, dehydration, hypokalemia, and achlorhydria. Which of the following neuroendocrine tumors can be responsible for these symptoms?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. VIPoma

The given clinical scenario is suggestive of VIPoma.

Vasoactive intestinal peptide-secreting tumors (VIPomas) are neuroendocrine tumors that secrete excessive amounts of vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP). The condition is known as Verner–Morrison syndrome or WDHA syndrome.

WDHA stands for:

* WD - Watery Diarrhea

* H – Hypokalemia

* A – Achlorhydria

Diagnosis can be made by the demonstration of an elevated plasma VIP level and the history of large-volume diarrhea.

Treatment includes correction of dehydration, hypokalemia, and electrolyte losses with fluid and electrolyte replacement. Long-acting somatostatin analogs such as octreotide and lanreotide are the drug of choice.

Pearl PF0939: Pancreatic Endocrine Neoplasms

Endocrine neoplasm

Syndrome

Glucagonoma

Mild diabetes mellitus, a characteristic skin rash (necrolytic migratory erythema), and anemia

Insulinoma

Clinically significant hypoglycemia

Gastrinoma

Peptic ulceration often unresponsive to therapy and in unusual locations such as the jejunum

Somatostatinoma

Diabetes mellitus, cholelithiasis, steatorrhea, and hypochlorhydria

VIPoma

Watery diarrhea, hypokalemia, achlorhydria, or WDHA syndrome

Pancreatic polypeptide-secreting endocrine tumors

Present as mass lesions as even high plasma levels of this hormone fail to cause symptoms

* Islet hyperplasia (previously known as nesidioblastosis) is seen in maternal diabetes, Beckwith–Wiedemann syndrome , and rare mutations in the β-cell K+-channel protein or sulfonylurea receptor.

* In maternal diabetes, the fetal islets respond to hyperglycemia by increasing their size and number. In the postnatal period, these hyperactive islets may be responsible for serious episodes of hypoglycemia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which adverse effect of Bleomycin is exacerbated by radiation exposure?
questions.explanation: Bleomycin is an antitumor antibiotic known for its dose-limiting pulmonary toxicity, which can manifest as interstitial pneumonitis or progressive pulmonary fibrosis. This risk is significantly exacerbated by concurrent or prior radiation exposure, a phenomenon sometimes called "radiation recall pneumonitis". The lung tissue is particularly vulnerable because it lacks significant levels of bleomycin hydrolase, the enzyme responsible for inactivating the drug. Regarding other options, bleomycin has minimal impact on the gastrointestinal tract (Option B) and is not associated with significant neurotoxicity (Option C), unlike drugs like vincristine. It also lacks the significant hepatotoxicity (Option D) seen with many other chemotherapeutic agents. Cumulative doses exceeding 400 units and supplemental oxygen therapy also increase the risk of lung damage. Therefore, monitoring pulmonary function via is essential when combining bleomycin with radiation

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.text: Post-dural puncture headache depends on all except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Timing of ambulation

Post-dural puncture headache (PDPH) is primarily related to CSF leakage through the dural hole, leading to intracranial hypotension.

•

Its incidence is strongly influenced by patient factors and technical factors, but early or delayed ambulation does not affect the risk of PDPH.

•

Studies have shown that prolonged bed rest after dural puncture does not reduce headache incidence, and early mobilisation is safe.

Why others are incorrect:

Option A: Younger age increases PDPH risk due to higher dural elasticity.

Option C: Pregnancy increases risk because of hormonal and anatomical factors.

Option D: Needle type (large gauge, cutting needles) significantly increases PDPH risk.

questions.subject: Paediatrics
questions.text: A 12-year-old child presents with short stature. On evaluation, bone age is found to be 10 years, and the upper segment to lower segment (US:LS) ratio is 1.1:1. There are no dysmorphic features, and the child is otherwise healthy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Constitutional delay of growth and puberty
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Constitutional delay of growth and puberty

Constitutional delay of growth and puberty (CDGP) is a common cause of short stature characterized by delayed bone age with otherwise normal body proportions and health.

• Bone age is delayed compared to chronological age
• Normal upper segment to lower segment ratio indicates proportionate short stature
• No dysmorphic features or systemic illness
• Growth velocity is usually normal, but puberty is delayed

Differentiation:

• Familial short stature: bone age matches chronological age
• Achondroplasia/chondrodysplasia: disproportionate short stature with abnormal body ratios
